messages:
Alex (Sales): AcmeProc pushed back on our SIG answers, specifically the BCP/DR block. They want a short, pasteable response for: RTO, RPO, backup cadence, failover steps, and evidence of DR tests. Can SRE + Legal help craft copy? :pray:

Priya (Solutions Eng): I can put together a short snippet. Quick question: Acme checked a box for "RTO <= 1 hour" in their form. Do we ever commit to that for any product?

Sam (SRE): Short: we don't offer a 1-hour contractual RTO for Hosted. Hosted = high-availability ops, automated routing, but no guaranteed RTO/RPO.

Sam (SRE): For Dedicated we have SLA tiers: Standard 99.9% / Premium 99.95% monthly uptime. Operational RTO targets for a full-environment failover are typically in the 2-4 hour window depending on customer topology and pre-provisioned warm pools.

Sam (SRE): Private (VPC/on-prem) = customer-managed. We provide runbooks and tools (snapshot tooling, warm-standby patterns). RTO/RPO are defined during onboarding and contract SOW.

Priya (Solutions Eng): Good. Can you give a concise backup/RPO line I can paste?

Sam (SRE): Backup/RPO bullets (one-liners):
- Hosted control plane metadata and logs: configurable retention (e.g., 90/365) per contract.
- Hosted customer request data: short-term persistence; not covered by a hosted RPO guarantee unless explicitly included in Dedicated backup add-on.
- Dedicated: we can offer point-in-time backups and retention SLAs; RPO depends on snapshot cadence (recommended: daily full + hourly increments to approach sub-hour RPO).
- Private: supports customer-controlled snapshots and replication; RPO based on customer config.

Priya (Solutions Eng): Failover steps (short):
1) Health detection and traffic routing away from impacted nodes/region
2) Cache/KV fallback where available (best-effort)
3) Promotion of warm-standby Dedicated pools if provisioned
4) DNS/edge failover for Private/Dedicated when configured
(Note: timing depends on topology and provisioning.)

Lena (Legal): Draft legal-safe paragraph for procurement form (pasteable):
"Redwood Inference operates a tiered service model. Hosted API deployments are operated for high availability and automated failover where feasible but do not include contractual RTO/RPO commitments. Dedicated capacity is covered by contractual uptime SLAs (99.9% standard, 99.95% premium) and documented recovery procedures; specific RTO/RPO values, backup cadences, and runbooks are set forth in the Service Addendum. Private deployments' recovery objectives are agreed case-by-case. Data is encrypted in transit and at rest and audit logging is available; backup retention and controls are defined in the agreement. All statements are subject to the Master Services Agreement."

Alex (Sales): Nice. They also want evidence: "Do you perform DR tests?" Can we provide something short and attachable?

Sam (SRE): Yes. Short evidence line: "We conduct quarterly DR tabletop exercises and annual live failover tests for Dedicated capacity; Private customers coordinate tests with their ops teams. We can provide a one-page summary of the most recent tabletop and associated action items upon request."

Priya (Solutions Eng): I'll bundle: (1) the legal-safe paragraph; (2) the backup/RPO bullets; (3) the failover steps; (4) a one-page DR summary offer. Will cc Legal.

Lena (Legal): Add final clause: "Subject to the terms of the Master Services Agreement and applicable Service Addendum." Also remove numeric RTO from Hosted language to avoid implying guarantee.

Alex (Sales): Action items: Priya send the pasteable answers + runbook excerpt to AcmeProc (cc Lena), Sam produce anonymized 12-month availability metrics for Dedicated, and Sam produce the 1-pager summarizing last DR tabletop.

deploy-bot: DR-test-scheduler scheduled: tabletop-2026-06-10 16:00 UTC (reminder 7d)

Priya (Solutions Eng): Sending draft to AcmeProc now. Will update thread when they reply. Thanks everyone :raised_hands:
